correctness.rationale: Read RESULT.md §§Source input–Proof, VERIFICATION.md, and the finite verifier (not executed). In the named two-modal signature an automorphism preserves the two equivalence relations separately. The sole two-point intersection singles out the top row, rightmost column and unordered corner pair. All other intersections determine one coordinate map (α(i),β(j)), with each permutation fixing ω. If the induced permutation of the corner pair is σ, clopenness of the two wings and the corner neighborhood conditions imply h(g₁) △ g_{σ(1)} is compact in X₀: each of the two differences is closed in X₀ and contained in a compact remainder. In the ambient compact square this compact set misses a whole tail rectangle at the deleted corner. For a=α⁻¹ and b=β⁻¹, in the fixed-corner case this gives a(j)≤b(j)<a(j+1) eventually. The increasing tail of a enumerates the complement of its finite initial image, hence has zero eventual shift; b is then eventually the identity as well. In the swapped case it gives a(j)>b(j)≥a(j+1) eventually, impossible in ω. Conversely a finite-support pair changes triangular membership only on finitely many compact coordinate strips; the differences are closed there and the map and inverse extend continuously fixing both corners. This proves sufficiency as well as necessity. Named Jónsson–Tarski duality and inversion give the asserted group isomorphism; finite support also gives countability and local finiteness, and no finite generating set can move infinitely many indices. The finite script is only a supplementary bounded check, not evidence for the topology or the infinite permutation argument.
